summary: Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, Marshall Sahlins studied at the University of Michigan (~1947–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954). He held posts at the University of Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (from 1973).

Marta Sernesi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Turin in 2007. Her career includes a post as a visiting professor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Martha Ann Selby is an Indologist who became professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026). She also held posts as professor and Department of South Asian Studies chair at Harvard University (attested 2026).

Philosopher Martha Nussbaum studied at Wellesley College, NYU, and Harvard, and under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Harvard, Oxford, and Brown, before joining the University of Chicago in 1995, later holding a visiting chair at Goethe University Frankfurt (2013).

Martin Baumann is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Leibniz University Hannover (~1988–1993) and completed his habilitation at the University of Leipzig (~1994–1999). In 2001, he became professor at the University of Lucerne.

Martin Brauen, a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies, studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Zurich. He held positions at the Ethnographic Museum of the University of Zurich (from 1975) and the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and Harvard (PhD 1975). He taught at Yokohama National University, the University of Tokyo, and held a long-term post at Princeton University (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Hamburg, Göttingen, Ryukoku University, Shandong University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He held academic posts at Bonn, Heidelberg, Deccan College (~1859–1866), and the University of Munich (from 1868).

Philosopher Martin Heidegger studied at the University of Freiburg (~1909–1916) under Heinrich Rickert. He held teaching posts at the University of Freiburg (1915–1923, 1936–1940) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Linguist and Indologist Martin Joachim Kümmel completed his MA, PhD, and habilitation at the University of Freiburg, also studying at Marburg. He served as an assistant at Freiburg (~1999–2008) and was appointed chairholder at the University of Jena in 2013.

Martin Kay worked in computational linguistics, having studied at the University of Cambridge (~1954–1958). He held positions at UC Irvine (~1969–1972), the Palo Alto Research Center (~1972–1984), UT Austin (~1982–1984), and Stanford University (~1984–2020).

Martin King Whyte, a specialist in sinology and sociology, studied at Cornell and Harvard (PhD 1971). He held positions at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and Harvard University (from 2000).

Martin Lehnert is a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Freiburg. He served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich (attested 2016).

Martin Lowenthal is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Orwin is a linguist who completed his studies at SOAS University of London between ~1988 and 1992. His career includes academic posts at SOAS University of London (~1992) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

Martin Riesebrodt studied at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (PhD 1973), and Munich (habilitation 1990). Working in religious studies and sociology, he held posts at the University of Chicago (1990–2014) and the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).

Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2004 under Barend Jan Terwiel. He held a post at Hamburg (attested 2004) and served on the Pali Text Society Council (attested 2026).

Martin Straube is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. As of 2026, he holds posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, the University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martin T. Adam specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied at CIHTS and McGill University (PhD attested 2002) under Richard P. Hayes and others. He also held a post as an instructor at McGill University.
